key_facts: Mangrove and tidal marsh vertical adjustment deficits are likely at 4 mm/yr relative sea-level rise and highly likely at 7 mm/yr.
Exposure to high RSLR increases strongly with warming and is relevant for coastal ecosystem persistence.
Tropical cyclones are a leading natural disturbance for mangroves.
Mangrove response depends strongly on cyclone intensity, recurrence, and site context.
Major cyclones (Category 3-5) dominate mangrove damage risk globally.
Category 4-5 cyclones contribute most global damage risk and regional risk shifts can diverge under warming.
Mangrove ecosystem services are globally important and conservation prioritization should consider ecosystem services.

contract_updates: Use RSLR thresholds informed by related work (4 and 7 mm/yr) as interpretable validation references.
Represent tropical cyclone hazard with emphasis on major/intense cyclone exposure rather than all storms equally.
Include scenario-specific comparison and geographically explicit hotspot identification relevant to conservation planning.
